## SECTION 2 — DATA QUALITY ASSESSMENT

This pack is materially usable, but I applied the following data-discipline corrections:

1. **Capex conflict — unresolved.** Filed capex is only $0.007B FY2025 (PP&E purchases). Vendor capex is $0.295B (42× higher). The pack says the filed figure excludes capitalized software; the vendor figure may include one-off acquisition-related items. I do **not** accept either as the right recurring number. My base case normalizes capex at **2% of revenue** and I show sensitivity to this driver.

2. **Working capital column is NOT operating working capital.** The pack’s “working capital” and “change in WC” use current assets **including cash and short-term investments**, so they are contaminated. I recomputed a non-cash operating WC proxy from filed components: receivables + inventory − current liabilities.

   | FY | Non-cash WC proxy |
   |---|---:|
   | 2022 | 0.231 + 0.100 − 0.131 = 0.200 |
   | 2023 | 0.233 + 0.128 − 0.112 = 0.249 |
   | 2024 | 0.288 + 0.142 − 0.139 = 0.291 |
   | 2025 | 0.426 + 0.176 − 0.177 = 0.425 |

   Incremental WC / revenue growth was ~23–35% in 2022–2025. I use **20% of revenue growth** in the forward model — an assumption, but not the raw pack figure.

3. **Net debt.** I use FY2025 long-term debt of $2.143B less FY2025 cash of $0.134B = **$2.009B net debt**. Section 6B shows current portion at $0.000B for FY2025, and Section 2 vendor total debt of $2.143B matches our LT-debt figure exactly. Short-term investments are held for 2019–2022 only; post-2022 they are absent from the pack and are treated as $0, which is the conservative direction.

4. **FY2025 GAAP operating margin is distorted.** The 2025 income statement includes a large anomality (likely acquired in-process R&D from Surf Bio/Elektrofi and/or other adjusted items): FY2025 operating income margin is only 33.6% vs 2024’s 54.3% and 2026 guided adjusted EBITDA ~66%. The forward model uses **normalized EBIT margins derived from 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance**, not the depressed 2025 GAAP margin.

5. **SBC is not an added-back item in my model.** I project EBIT on a GAAP basis, so SBC is already inside the EBIT margin. This is deliberate and conservative.

6. **No segment data, no Q&A, no reliable total-debt sum.** Where these gaps matter, I explicitly carry them as uncertainties.

## SECTION 3 — VALUATION ENGINE SELECTION

I selected a **two-stage FCFF-DCF** because:

- HALO’s economics are royalty-heavy; margins are high and scale is still increasing.
- The company has explicit 2026–2028 financial guidance, making a three-year explicit-fade model the natural backbone.
- The balance-sheet leverage is moderate, so a WACC-based FCFF enterprise model is appropriate; I remove net debt to get equity value.
- Earnings multiples are unreliable for this company because GAAP net income is currently distorted by one-time deal costs and because the earnings power is forward-looking.

I reject:
- **Dividend discount model** — no dividend.
- **Relative value as primary** — useful only as cross-check.
- **Single-trailing FCF perpetual** — the company is growing rapidly, and management has provided explicit forward guidance.

**Business model.** Halozyme is a royalty-tollbooth drug-delivery platform:
- **ENHANZE** (recombinant human hyaluronidase, rHuPH20) enables subcutaneous delivery of high-volume biologics. Partners (J&J/DARZALEX SC, Roche/PHESGO, Ocrevus SC, argenx/VYVGART Hytrulo, J&J/RYBREVANT) formulate their drugs with Halozyme's enzyme; Halozyme earns mid-single-digit royalties on partner product sales.
- **2025 acquisitions:** Elektrofi/Hypercon and Surf Bio (hyperconcentration technologies), plus autoinjector supply — extending the royalty runway into the mid-2040s. **[Actual — company PR / MarketBeat write-up of investor call, 2026-01-29]**

**Moat quality score (my assessment): High but narrowing.**
1. **Switching costs are real.** Once a partner drug is reformulated and approved with ENHANZE for Phase 3, switching to a competing enzyme would require re-approval — effectively a permanent per-product lock. This is a genuine tollbooth with 80%+ gross margin. **[Actual — company model; also noted in pack's web brief]**
2. **Patent fragility is the hole in the moat.** On 2026-05-12 and 2026-05-18 the PTAB issued Final Written Decisions invalidating two of Halozyme's PH20 patents (US 11,952,600; US 12,152,262), and denied institution on a third (US 12,371,685) — all in Merck's PGR challenges relating to **Keytruda Qlex** (pembrolizumab with Merck's own hyaluronidase). 12 more PGRs remain pending; a New Jersey infringement case (2:25-cv-03179) is ongoing. **[Estimate — law-firm/legal-BSJ report, 2026-05-22; legal outcome is [Actual] as reported by Venable/BiologicsHQ]**
   - **Why this does NOT kill existing royalties:** ENHANZE royalties are contractual — partners pay for Halozyme's enzyme and license regardless of patent status. The invalidated patents mainly threaten (a) future royalties from *new* non-licensed users like Merck, and (b) future deal pricing power.
   - **Financial stake at issue:** Keytruda Qlex launched Sept 2025, ~$40M 2025 sales, ramping; a notional 1–3% Halozyme royalty would be worth only $0.4–1.2M on 2025 sales, but $100–300M/yr if Keytruda SC reaches $10B. **Base case assumes $0 from this dispute — the PTAB has already ruled against Halozyme.**
3. **Customer concentration is extreme.** Top partners (J&J, Roche, argenx) likely account for >70% of royalty revenue. DARZALEX SC 2025 sales: $14.3B; VYVGART Hytrulo: $4.15B. **[Actual — company statements]**
4. **DARZALEX IV patent cliff (~2029–2031) is the key long-term risk** to the largest royalty driver; J&J's SC conversion helps offset biosimilar erosion of the IV form, but US biosimilar entry against the SC form will eventually come. My base case decelerates growth into the early 2030s accordingly.

**Moat rating: 6/10 — real switching-cost moat, but patent and concentration vulnerabilities that a 14.5% short interest already signals the market is aware of.**

## SECTION 1 — BUSINESS UNDERSTANDING

**What HALO is.** HALO licenses its proprietary ENHANZE® platform — recombinant human hyaluronidase (rHuPH20) — to large pharma, enabling subcutaneous injection of large-volume biologics (converting IV infusions to 5-10 minute SC injections). The company collects royalties (typically mid-single-digit % of partner product sales, per Q1-2026 transcript: "mid-single-digit royalties with the opportunity for escalators"). A second platform, Hypercon® (high-concentration SC), is earlier-stage with first Phase I starts expected 1H-2027 and $1B royalty revenue projected by the mid-2030s (Q1-2026 call).

**Revenue components (order of importance):**
1. **Royalties** — ~55-60% of revenue (2026E royalties to exceed $1.0B vs ~$0.75B in 2025 per mgmt guidance; Q2-2026 royalty revenue $307.7M, +50% YoY).
2. **Product sales** — bulk rHuPH20 (API) and auto-injectors (the latter lower-margin).
3. **Collaboration/upfront/milestone payments** — lumpy; 2026 is heavy (GSK ADC deal, Vertex Hypercon, Oruka Hypercon signed early 2026).

**Partner concentration (computed from Q2-2026 royalties of $307.7M):**
- DARZALEX SC (J&J): $129M, 42% of royalties; +26% YoY
- VYVGART Hytrulo (argenx): $46.3M, 15%; +119% YoY
- PHESGO (Roche): $30.2M, 10%; +25% YoY
- Top 3 ≈ 67% of royalty revenue.

**Moat.** The ENHANZE toll-booth is a real switching-cost moat: once a partner's drug is formulated with rHuPH20 and reaches Phase III, reformulation is economically irrational absent patent invalidation.
